13. Mr. Khair Ejaj Masood, the learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondents made submissions in support of the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division. He submits that, on 19.08.1977, the respondent No.1 as plaintiff filed Title Suit No.117 of 1977 for Specific Performance of Contract. According to the contract, Exhibit-1, the price was fixed at Tk.l8,800/- of which Tk.17,000/- was paid as earnest money, and, the rest was fixed to be paid within two years, and, the agreement also contain a default clause. The plaintiff in his deposition has clearly stated that, he made the offer of the rest of the contract money within the stipulated time of two years and, thereafter, issued a written notice on 01.08.1977, and, on the refusal by the defendant No.1, Nirendra. Chandra Das, the suit was filed. In deposition, the P.W.1 categorically stated that, he made the offer within the stipulated period, and, this statement of the P.W. 1 was not challenged by cross-examination, hence, this statement remained uncontroverted, and, would be deemed to have been admitted. Under Article 113 of the Limitation Act, the period of limitation in a suit for Specific Performance of Contract is 3 years from the date fixed for performance. This view finds support from the case reported in 42 DL R (AD)63. Moreover, in a suit for Specific Performance of Contract, time is not the essence of contract specially when the suit was filed within time, and, this view finds support from the 5 MLR AD 189 case. He further submits that, the plaintiff has filed the original Kabla executed by Omiva in favour of the plaintiff and these registered kabalas carry a presumption of their correctness and the documents (Exhibits 2-4) filed from the custody of the plaintiff lend support to the genuineness of the agreement. From Exhibit-6, it appears that, the decree was obtained against the defendant No.1, Nirendra Chandra as by suppression of summon, and, the same is apparent from the service return (Exhibit-10) which shows Omiya Ghosh has remained untraced, and, the application for service of summon under Order 5 Rule 20 was prayed for, but, order sheet (Exhibit-9) shows that, the, Court passed no order, and order dated 09.02.197 further shows that, the suit was fixed for Service Return which was not received, and, by the same order, the Court found that, the service return has been received, and, fixed on 03.03.1978 for exparte hearing without giving any chance for filing written statement. The Court was not competent to proceed for an exparte decree. In such circumstances, thus, fraud is apparent in bringing about the exparte decree. Hanes, the, High Court Division rightly passed the impugned judgment. Therefore, he prays for dismissal of the instant appeal. 

 27. The findings of the appellate court and the High Court. Division on service of summons in Title Suit No. 148 of 1977, and the submissions made on behalf of the respondents in this regard are totally misconceived and wrong which is apparent from the entire Order Sheet of Title Suit No. 148 of 1977. Order No. 6 dated 29.09.1977 Order No. 8 dated 19.12.1977 and Order No. 10 dated 09.02.1978 clearly show that service of summons was effected by Registered Post with AD, and AD was received by the court.
